references.text: The Lord will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. This is a parallel threat of scattering among the nations as punishment for disobedience.
Moses prophesies that the Lord will scatter the Israelites among the peoples, and only a small remnant will remain. The same theme of exile and dispersion.
Ezekiel describes how God will do what has never been done before because of Israel's abominations, including scattering. Fulfillment of the threat in Leviticus.
God says He will scatter the people to all winds and pursue them with the sword. A direct echo of both the scattering and the sword drawn after them.
Jeremiah quotes the Lord's threat to scatter the people among nations they did not know, and send the sword after them. Almost a word-for-word parallel.
Jeremiah prophesies that the whole land will become a desolate waste. Fulfillment of the threat that the land would lie desolate.
Isaiah describes how the land is ruined, cities burned with fire, and foreigners devouring the land. Fulfillment of the prophecy about destroyed cities.
Nehemiah confesses that God scattered the Israelites among the peoples as He had threatened. Acknowledgment of the fulfillment of this prophecy.
The context in the same chapter where God threatens to destroy the cities and make the land a desolate waste, so that enemies are horrified.
Stephen quotes the prophets saying that God led the people into exile beyond Babylon. New Testament confirmation of the exile as punishment.
